info.title: LegendKeeper API
info.description:
REST API for the [LegendKeeper](https://www.legendkeeper.com) world-building platform.

Every endpoint follows one response contract: a single object is returned bare,
a collection is `{ data: [...], hasMore, nextCursor }`, and a delete returns `204`.

## Blocks and rows

Page content is a tree of typed blocks (`getDocumentBlocks`). Every block carries a stable `id`.
A write that omits an id gets one minted. `insertBlock` and `replaceBlock` keep a requested id, and answer `409`
`DUPLICATE_ID` with the field path when another block of the document already uses it; `replaceBlock` may reuse
the ids of the subtree it replaces. Two equal block ids in one body answer `400` `VALIDATION_ERROR` at the second. Legacy
documents whose blocks lack ids become addressable after one `assignBlockIds` call.

`replaceDocumentBlocks` replaces the whole tree. `insertBlock` appends at the end or takes one of
`after`, `before`, `parent`; `replaceBlock` keeps the block id; `updateBlock` changes own fields;
`moveBlock` relocates a subtree; `deleteBlock` removes it. Content the block model cannot
express is returned as `unsupported` and survives a replace only when echoed by id.
Every write validates the resulting document and answers `400` with `VALIDATION_ERROR`,
`UNSUPPORTED_KIND` or `INVALID_CONTENT` and the offending block path. Nothing is written in that case.

Key-value data lives in three places and shares one row shape at each:
a sidebar property of kind `keyValue` (`/properties/{propertyId}/rows`), a `keyValue` block
(`/blocks/{blockId}/rows`), and a property inside an infobox
(`/blocks/{infoboxId}/properties/{propertyId}/rows`). Rows are ordered by `rank`.
An infobox row is a property; `/blocks/{infoboxId}/properties` takes the same body
as `createProperty`.

Every block, row and infobox-property response carries the document `version`
(also the `ETag` header). Send it back as `If-Match` to fail with `412` instead of
overwriting a change made since you read.

## Boards

A board document holds tldraw 3.9 records: pages, shapes, bindings and assets (`getBoardContent`).
Reads return the records as stored, in tldraw's own record shape, so tldraw's `TLShape`,
`TLBinding` and `TLAsset` types describe them. Writes (`createBoardShapes`, `updateBoardShapes`,
`deleteBoardShapes`, `replaceBoardContent`) are batched and atomic, and every record is validated
with tldraw's validators against the schema the app's board view uses. Each record is stored
separately, so a write merges with concurrent edits made in the app, record by record.

## Field limits

Every request field declares its limit as `maxLength`, `maxItems` or `maxProperties`, and nesting is limited
to 64 levels. A value past a limit answers `400` with `code: "VALIDATION_ERROR"` and the field path.
Limits apply to writes. Content created in the app that exceeds a limit reads back unchanged; a write that
sends it back, such as a whole-block replace, answers `400` at that value.

## Errors

Every 4xx and 5xx response body is `{ message, code, requestId, errors? }`. `code` is one of the
values below and fixes the status. `message` is human-readable and stable in meaning, not in wording.
`errors` appears only on 400 responses: one entry `{ path, message }` per failing field or block, with a
dotted `path` (`block.children[0].level`). `KIND_MISMATCH` names a path entity rather than a body field
and carries no `errors`.

| Status | Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | The body or query fails the schema; `errors[].path` names each field. |
| 400 | `INVALID_CONTENT` | The block tree is schema-valid but the editor cannot hold it. |
| 400 | `UNSUPPORTED_KIND` | Creating an `unsupported` block or property, or echoing an unsupported id the document does not hold. |
| 400 | `KIND_MISMATCH` | The target document, block or calendar is not a kind the route accepts (rows on a block or property that is not keyValue; blocks on a document that is not a page; pins on a document that is not a map; events on a document that is not a timeline; an update or delete of a built-in calendar). |
| 401 | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | No credential, or an unknown, revoked or expired key. |
| 402 | `SUBSCRIPTION_LAPSED` | The project owner's plan does not allow the write. |
| 402 | `PAID_PLAN_REQUIRED` | The project owner is not on a paid plan, which API keys require; a trial does not count. |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | The caller is not a member with the required role. |
| 403 | `WRONG_PROJECT` | The key's project is not the path's project. |
| 403 | `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` | The key lacks a scope the operation requires. |
| 403 | `FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE` | The request uses a field of a feature that is not available yet; send it without that field. |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | A missing entity, including a placement anchor. |
| 405 | `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` | The path exists; the method does not. |
| 409 | `DUPLICATE_ID` | A supplied id already exists. |
| 409 | `AMBIGUOUS` | A block id occurs more than once in a legacy document. |
| 409 | `ALREADY_DELETED` | The entity is already deleted. |
| 409 | `HAS_CHILDREN` | The resource has child resources that are not deleted; pass `cascade=true` to delete them with it. |
| 409 | `NOT_DELETED` | The entity to restore is not deleted. |
| 409 | `PARENT_DELETED` | The resource's parent is deleted; restore the parent first. |
| 409 | `IN_PROGRESS` | A prior operation on the entity has not finished. |
| 409 | `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` | The idempotency key was used for a different request. |
| 409 | `TOO_MANY_PENDING_INVITES` | The project holds as many pending invites as it may; revoke some before inviting more. |
| 412 | `VERSION_MISMATCH` | `If-Match` does not equal the current version. |
| 422 | `DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE` | The write would grow the document past its size limit. |
| 413 | `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | The body exceeds the route's limit. |
| 413 | `STORAGE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` | The project owner's storage quota is reached. |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | A key or project tier is exhausted; see `Retry-After`. |
| 429 | `UPLOAD_RATE_EXCEEDED` | The upload tier is exhausted. |
| 500 | `INTERNAL` | Unexpected failure; the body carries only the code, a fixed message and `requestId`, which identifies the server log line. |

## Identifiers

`createResource`, `createLane`, `createEvent` and `createFeature` accept an optional `id`. An id must be a lowercase letter followed by 7 or 23 lowercase letters or digits (a cuid2 id of 8 or 24 characters):
the formats LegendKeeper itself generates. Any other value answers `400` `VALIDATION_ERROR` at `id`. An id that is
already taken answers `409` `DUPLICATE_ID` and nothing is created. A resource id is taken when any resource of the
project has it, including a deleted resource, which stays restorable from the trash. A lane, event or feature id
is taken when the same timeline or map already has it.

A client-chosen id lets an importer keep one stable identity per record and find it again on the next sync with
`getResource`, instead of matching by name. Idempotency keys expire after 24 hours and are not a re-sync mechanism.
A created resource's documents are its `documents`, in the order sent; each is reached through the resource id.

## Resource order

Siblings in the resource tree are ordered by `rank`, a fractional index compared as a plain string. `createResource`
and `moveResource` compute the rank with the same jittered fractional-indexing functions the app uses: after the
last sibling by default, or between the anchor and its neighbour for `after` and `before`. The new rank never
equals the rank of an existing sibling. Resources created or moved through older clients can share a rank; placing
after or before one of them places the resource after or before every sibling that shares that rank.

## Templates

A template is a resource under the virtual root `templates`. `templates` is a reserved id: no resource has it,
and it is not returned by getResource. A top-level template has `parentId` `templates`. A resource under a
template is a template too, and its `parentId` is that template's id. Search and collections do not return
templates.

Templates are read, updated, moved and deleted with the resource operations. These operations also take the
`templates` id:

| Operation | `templates` as |
| --- | --- |
| `listResources` | Without `parentId`, templates are listed with the other resources. `parentId=templates` lists the top-level templates. |
| `createResource`, `createManyResources` | `parentId: "templates"` creates a top-level template. |
| `moveResource` | `parentId: "templates"` makes the resource a top-level template; `parentId: null` moves it back to the root. |

Three operations cover templates without the `templates` id:

| Operation | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `listTemplates` | Lists every template at any depth, paginated. |
| `saveResourceAsTemplate` | Copies a resource, and with `includeChildren` its descendants, into a new top-level template. The resource does not change. |
| `createResourceFromTemplate` | Copies a template, and with `includeChildren` its descendants, into a new resource. The name drops the word `Template`. |

Only a project admin may create a resource under `templates`, move one there, or call `saveResourceAsTemplate`.
A copy takes the source's fields, properties and documents with their content, under new ids. Mentions in the
copied content keep pointing at the resources they named in the source.

## Request ids

Every response carries an `x-request-id` header; every error body carries the same value as `requestId`.
A client-supplied `x-request-id` is echoed when it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$`; otherwise a fresh id
is minted and the supplied value is ignored. The server log line for the request carries the same id, so
quote it when reporting a problem.

## Idempotency

Every POST accepts an optional `Idempotency-Key` header of 1–255 characters from `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -`.
A malformed key answers `400` `VALIDATION_ERROR` with `Idempotency-Key` in `errors[].path`. Keys are scoped
to the API key, or to the user for a session, so two callers never share one.

The first request with a key runs and its response is kept for 24 hours. A repeat with the same key, method,
path and body returns the kept status and body without running the write again, with `Idempotent-Replay: true`
and `Idempotent-Original-Request-Id` naming the first request; its own `x-request-id` is new. A repeat while the
first is still running answers `409` `IN_PROGRESS`; retry it. The same key on a different request answers
`409` `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`.

2xx and 4xx responses are kept, except the refusals answered before any write: `400` `VALIDATION_ERROR`,
`401`, `403` and `404`. A refusal, a 5xx or 429 response, or a body over 64 KB is not kept: the key is released
and a request with the key runs, so a corrected request can reuse the key. PATCH, PUT and DELETE ignore the header.

## Rate limits

API-key requests are counted in the tiers below. A request that exhausts any tier answers `429` with
`code: "RATE_LIMITED"`.

| Scope | Window | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Writes (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE), per key | 1 minute | 120 |
| Writes (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE), per key | 1 hour | 3,000 |
| All requests, per key | 1 minute | 300 |
| All requests, per key | 1 hour | 6,000 |
| All requests, per key | 1 day | 60,000 |
| All requests, per project across keys | 1 hour | 12,000 |

Tiers are consumed in the order write minute, write hour, key minute, key hour, key day, project hour; a read skips the write tiers.
Every response to an authenticated request carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and
`X-RateLimit-Reset` (a Unix time in seconds) for the tier with the fewest requests remaining, so a write reports
the write tier once it is the tightest. A `429` carries them for the tier that rejected, plus `Retry-After` in
seconds. A request refused before it is counted (a 400 schema error, 401, 402, 403 or 405) carries none. The
per-project tier is keyed on the key's project, so every key of a project draws on it.

bearerAuth.description: Project API key. Create one in Project Settings → Developers → API Keys. A key acts with the lower of its own role and its creator's project role, and only in its own project: a request that names another project answers 403 WRONG_PROJECT. An API key has at most the ADMIN role, and is accepted only on /api/v3 routes: the app's /api/v1 and /api/v2 routes answer 403 FORBIDDEN to a key. Keys need the project owner to be on a paid plan (a trial does not count): creating a key, and every request a key authenticates, answers 402 PAID_PLAN_REQUIRED while the owner is not.

BoardJsonValue.description: Any JSON value: a string of up to 100,000 characters, a number, a boolean, null, an array of up to 10,000 values, or an object of up to 10,000 keys of up to 256 characters. Arrays and objects nest at most 32 levels.

JsonValue.description: Any JSON value: a string of up to 100,000 characters, a number, a boolean, null, an array of up to 256 values, or an object of up to 256 keys of up to 256 characters. Arrays and objects nest at most 8 levels.

assetId.description: The image asset in the project's library whose `url` is the map's image. null when no image asset readable by the caller has that url: the asset was deleted, it is hidden and the caller is not a project admin, or the map uses a legacy tiled map.

url.description: The URL of the map's image. null for a legacy tiled map, which has no single image file.

width.description: The image width in pixels.

bounds.description: `[[south, west], [north, east]]`, the `[lat, lng]` corners the image covers. `north` and `west` are 0 at the image's top-left corner; `south` is negative and `east` is positive.

MapImage.description: The image of a map document and its coordinate frame. Feature `pos` values are `[lat, lng]` in this frame, the frame the app uses when a feature is placed by clicking the map. A pixel `(x, y)` of the image, counted in pixels from its top-left corner, is at `pos = [north - y * (north - south) / height, west + x * (east - west) / width]`, which is `[-y / 2^z, x / 2^z]` with `z = ceil(log2(max(width, height) / 256))`. A `pos` converts back with `x = (lng - west) * width / (east - west)` and `y = (north - lat) * height / (north - south)`. The SDK exports this conversion as `pixelToPos` and `posToPixel`.

color.description: Text color, as `#RRGGBB`.

highlight.description: Highlight color drawn behind the text, as `#RRGGBB`.

color.description: Text color, as `#RRGGBB`.

highlight.description: Highlight color drawn behind the text, as `#RRGGBB`.

ImageProperty.description: An image property by `url`. The URL is the `url` of an image asset of this project (upload with createImageUpload and createImageAsset). Any other URL, including an image asset of another project, answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming the field, unless the same document, resource or board already holds that URL in an image field. A `data:` or `blob:` URI answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming the field: documents hold no inline image data. Upload the image (createImageUpload, createImageAsset) and reference its URL. `fill: true` draws the image edge to edge with no frame or title, as the app's "Fill block" option does.

color.description: Fill color of the meter as `#RRGGBB`, or `none` to use the block tint. With `none` and no block tint the meter is drawn `#3B82F6`. Absent, `none`.

FilterPredicate.description: A collection filter. `composite` combines `filters` with `and`, `or` or `not`. Nesting through `children`, `rows` and filter `filters` is limited to 64 levels; deeper input answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

EmbedProperty.description: An embedded player property. A `data:` or `blob:` URI answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming the field: documents hold no inline image data. Upload the image (createImageUpload, createImageAsset) and reference its URL.

MapViewport.description: The view a map opens at: `center` as `[lat, lng]` in the map's coordinate frame, the frame of a feature's `pos`, and the Leaflet `zoom` level.

MapProperty.description: An interactive map property. `resourceId` and `documentId` name a `map` document of this project that the caller can read. A resource or document that does not exist, is deleted, is hidden from the caller, belongs to another project or is not a `map` document answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming the field, unless the same document or resource already holds that map. Name both ids or neither; a map with neither is an empty block that the app shows as "Link a map". `viewport` is the view the map opens at; omit it to center at zoom 4, or at the map's deepest zoom when that is lower, on a pin of the map whose link points to the resource holding the map. `displayHeight` is the height in pixels, 150 to 800; the app draws 200 when it is omitted. `fill: true` draws the map edge to edge and hides the title whatever `isTitleHidden` says.

PropertyBlock.description: A sidebar or infobox property: a structured block kind plus the property envelope (`rank`, `title`, `isTitleHidden`, `isHidden`). A property the public model cannot express reads as `kind: "unsupported"` with its id and envelope. A property is laid out by the infobox or sidebar that holds it, so it carries neither `layout` nor `width`. Nesting through `children`, `rows` and filter `filters` is limited to 64 levels; deeper input answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

type.description: The document type, as on Document: `page`, `board`, `map`, `time` or `blank`.

ListedDocument.description: A document as listed on a ResourceListItem.

iconColor.description: Fill color of this resource's map pins. Also tints its cards and graph nodes. Written as `#RRGGBB`; a resource from an import or an older version may hold another CSS color string. Null when no color is stored.

aliases.description: Alternative names of the resource, as on getResource.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, ending in `Z`.

updatedAt.description: ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, ending in `Z`.

iconShape.description: The shape drawn behind the glyph on a map pin, or `none` for the glyph alone.

iconSize.description: The size of the pin shape. Absent when `iconShape` is `none`.

documents.description: The resource's documents, ordered by name. Deleted documents are left out, and so are hidden documents for a caller who is not a project admin. Read a document by id for its content and settings.

ResourceListItem.description: A resource as listed: identity, icon, tags, aliases, rank and its documents' ids, names and types, enough to compare a page of resources with a local copy without reading each one. Read a resource by id for its properties, permissions and lock state.

hasMore.description: True when more items exist beyond this page.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null.

ErrorCode.description: The closed set of error codes. Each code has one status; the Errors section lists them.

message.description: Human-readable. Stable in meaning, not in wording.

requestId.description: The same value as the `x-request-id` response header. Quote it when reporting a problem.

errors.description: On 400 responses only: one entry per failing field or block; path is dotted (`block.children[0].level`). A `KIND_MISMATCH` response carries no `errors`.

Error.description: The body of every 4xx and 5xx response.

resourceId.description: The resource that holds the source timeline.

TimelineSource.description: A timeline (`time`) document that another timeline chains as a source. listLanes and listEvents on the chaining timeline include the lanes and events of its sources, and of their sources in turn.

deletedAt.description: ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, ending in `Z`.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, ending in `Z`.

updatedAt.description: ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, ending in `Z`.

calendarId.description: On a timeline (`time`) document, the id of the calendar its dates render in, as listed by listCalendars. Absent when the timeline has no calendar assigned; it then renders in the Gregorian calendar, as it does when the id names a deleted calendar. Absent on other document types.

sources.description: On a timeline (`time`) document, the timelines it chains, in order; empty when it chains none. A reference to a timeline the caller cannot read, because its resource is unreachable, it is hidden from a caller who is not a project admin, or it or its resource is deleted, is left out. Absent on other document types.

Document.description: A document of a resource. `type` is `page`, `board`, `map`, `time` or `blank`. A new resource's first document is `blank`. The first write of page blocks, board records, map features or timeline lanes to a `blank` document converts it to a `page`, `board`, `map` or `time` document and keeps its name, as picking a type for a blank document in the app does; a write that is refused or changes nothing leaves it `blank`, and reads never convert it. Once converted, the document answers 400 KIND_MISMATCH to writes of another type. A map document carries `mapImage` in the responses of getDocument, createDocument and updateDocument: its image and coordinate frame, or null when it has no image. listDocuments and getResource do not include `mapImage`. A timeline document carries `sources` in the responses of listDocuments, getDocument, createDocument and updateDocument; getResource does not include `sources`.

iconColor.description: Fill color of this resource's map pins. Also tints its cards and graph nodes. Written as `#RRGGBB`; a resource from an import or an older version may hold another CSS color string.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, ending in `Z`.

updatedAt.description: ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, ending in `Z`.

iconShape.description: The shape drawn behind the glyph on a map pin, or `none` for the glyph alone.

iconSize.description: The size of the pin shape. Absent when `iconShape` is `none`.

Resource.description: A resource. `properties` are its sidebar properties as PropertyBlocks. `iconSize` is absent when `iconShape` is `none`, and both are absent when no shape is stored; the app then draws a medium `pin`. A shape stored by the app in an older format reads as the app draws it: a glyph-only shape reads as `none`, and any other shape outside these values reads as `pin` and `medium`.

type.description: The document type: `page`, `board`, `map`, `time` or `blank`. Defaults to `page` when `blocks` is sent, otherwise to `blank`.

name.description: The document name, 1–500 characters. Defaults to `Main`.

calendarId.description: For a timeline (`time`) document, the id of a calendar from listCalendars, custom or built-in. An id that names no calendar in the project, or a `calendarId` with any other type, answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR at `documents[i].calendarId`.

blocks.description: The content of a `page` document as Blocks, validated as replaceDocumentBlocks validates them. Blocks with any other type answer 400 VALIDATION_ERROR at `documents[i].blocks`.

ResourceDocumentParams.description: A document of a new resource.

parentId.description: The parent resource. Omitted, the resource is created at the root. `templates` creates a top-level template. An unknown or deleted id answers 404 NOT_FOUND. A caller who is not a project admin must name a resource they can edit (Can Edit or Full Access), and cannot name `templates`.

iconGlyph.description: FontAwesome icon name (e.g., "crown", "dog", "snowflake"). See fontawesome.com/icons for valid names. An unknown name answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

iconColor.description: Fill color of this resource's map pins, as `#RRGGBB`. Also tints its cards and graph nodes. Defaults to `#C49454`.

iconShape.description: The shape drawn behind the glyph on a map pin: `pin`, `diamond`, `flag`, `marker`, `shield`, `circle`, `banner` or `arch`, or `none` for the glyph alone. Any other value answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR at the field. Omitted while `iconSize` is sent, it is `pin`. A resource created with neither `iconShape` nor `iconSize` has `iconShape` `none`.

isHidden.description: `true` creates the resource hidden. Only a project admin may create a hidden resource; a caller who is not answers 403 FORBIDDEN.

url.description: The banner image URL. The URL is the `url` of an image asset of this project (upload with createImageUpload and createImageAsset). Any other URL, including an image asset of another project, answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming the field, unless the same document, resource or board already holds that URL in an image field. A `data:` or `blob:` URI answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming the field: documents hold no inline image data. Upload the image (createImageUpload, createImageAsset) and reference its URL.

id.description: Optional client-chosen id: a lowercase letter followed by 7 or 23 lowercase letters or digits (a cuid2 id of 8 or 24 characters). See Identifiers. A malformed id answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. An id already used by a resource of the project, including a deleted one, answers 409 DUPLICATE_ID.

documents.description: 1–5 documents, created in this order. Omitted, the resource starts with one `blank` document named `Main`, which its first typed write converts.

iconSize.description: The size of the pin shape: `medium` or `small`. Ignored when `iconShape` is `none`. Any other value answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR at the field. Omitted while `iconShape` is sent, it is `medium`.

after.description: Id of a sibling under the same parent. The resource is placed directly after it. Mutually exclusive with `before`.

before.description: Id of a sibling under the same parent. The resource is placed directly before it. Mutually exclusive with `after`.

ResourceBatch.description: The created resources, in the order of the request.

resources.description: 1–100 resources to create, each a ResourceCreateParams, created in this order. An item may name an earlier item of the same batch as its `parentId` when that earlier item has an `id`; such an item is placed after its earlier siblings in the batch and cannot use `after` or `before`. A `parentId` that names a later item answers 404 NOT_FOUND.

templateId.description: The template to copy: a resource under the `templates` root, at any depth. A resource that is not a template answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. An unknown or deleted id, or one the caller cannot view, answers 404 NOT_FOUND.

id.description: Optional client-chosen id for the new resource: a lowercase letter followed by 7 or 23 lowercase letters or digits (a cuid2 id of 8 or 24 characters). See Identifiers. An id already used by a resource of the project answers 409 DUPLICATE_ID.

name.description: Name of the new resource. Omitted, it is the template's name with the word `Template` removed.

parentId.description: The parent of the new resource, as in createResource. Omitted, the resource is created at the root. An unknown or deleted id answers 404 NOT_FOUND.

includeChildren.description: `true` also copies the template's descendants the caller can view, keeping their tree. Default false. A copy holds at most 100 resources; a larger template answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

after.description: Id of a sibling under the same parent. The resource is placed directly after it. Mutually exclusive with `before`.

before.description: Id of a sibling under the same parent. The resource is placed directly before it. Mutually exclusive with `after`.

id.description: Optional client-chosen id for the new template: a lowercase letter followed by 7 or 23 lowercase letters or digits (a cuid2 id of 8 or 24 characters). See Identifiers. An id already used by a resource of the project answers 409 DUPLICATE_ID.

name.description: Name of the new template. Omitted, it is the resource's name.

includeChildren.description: `true` also copies the resource's descendants the caller can view, keeping their tree. Default false. A copy holds at most 100 resources; a larger tree answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

after.description: Id of a sibling under the same parent. The resource is placed directly after it. Mutually exclusive with `before`.

before.description: Id of a sibling under the same parent. The resource is placed directly before it. Mutually exclusive with `after`.

iconGlyph.description: FontAwesome icon name (e.g., "crown", "dog", "snowflake"). See fontawesome.com/icons for valid names. An unknown name answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

iconColor.description: Fill color of this resource's map pins, as `#RRGGBB`. Also tints its cards and graph nodes.

iconShape.description: The shape drawn behind the glyph on a map pin: `pin`, `diamond`, `flag`, `marker`, `shield`, `circle`, `banner` or `arch`, or `none` for the glyph alone. Any other value answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR at the field. Sent without `iconSize`, the stored `iconSize` is kept, or `medium` when none is stored.

isHidden.description: Only project admins may change `isHidden`. A change by a caller who is not a project admin answers 403 FORBIDDEN.

url.description: The banner image URL. The URL is the `url` of an image asset of this project (upload with createImageUpload and createImageAsset). Any other URL, including an image asset of another project, answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming the field, unless the same document, resource or board already holds that URL in an image field. A `data:` or `blob:` URI answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming the field: documents hold no inline image data. Upload the image (createImageUpload, createImageAsset) and reference its URL.

permissions.description: Access levels keyed by a role (`MEMBER`, `ADMIN` or `OWNER`) or a user id. A level is 0 No Access, 1 Can Read, 2 Can Edit, 3 Full Access, 4 defer to the role or 5 inherit from the parent. Entries not sent keep their value.
